extracted.intended_audience: general readers and policymakers following NATO summit, defense and Cold War news
extracted.subtask_description: A news report covering the NATO summit in Paris and related Cold War defense/foreign-policy developments, including policy proposals, technical/missile program debates, and allied reactions. Summarizes positions of leaders, numbered policy recommendations, and technical/organizational concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kennan: reassess Western foreign policy and avoid absolutism
rubrics_metrics.description: Call for a reassessment of Western foreign policy toward the Soviet Union, possible withdrawal of East and West forces in Europe, an end to the 'hopeless exertions' of the nuclear race; open the West to a 'new wind' and brace for scorn and hostility from communism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not give up unilateral nuclear deterrent, nor 'stop strengthening NATO forces in Europe'—but avoid strengthening NATO 'in such a way as to prejudice the chances for an eventual reduction, by peaceful negotiation, of the danger of an all-out war.' Urged 'piecemeal removal, by negotiation, of the major sources of military danger,' avoid pursuit of absolute security, and assume certain risks so that greater evils may be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serrano: system of coordination among NATO, SEATO and Baghdad Pact
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal for 'a system of coordination' among the three anti-Red alliances (NATO, SEATO, Baghdad Pact) to meet the 'new peril' of Russian missile and satellite advances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial suggestions for closer working included: (1) a system to exchange military, economic and cultural information; (2) a pool of technical talents; (3) a scheme of economic collaboration; (4) agreement on development of essential resources needed by member nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: WEU coordinated arms production and standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that Western European Union (WEU) pursue a program toward coordinated arms production to achieve greater efficiency and cheaper costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create an armaments commission to standardize weapons and parcel out production on a basis of efficiency among member nations; standardization and assigned production lines to streamline armaments and lower costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: NATO: participation in a NATO atomic stockpile
rubrics_metrics.description: United States to participate in a NATO atomic stockpile; the U.S. would supply an atomic stockpile to NATO according to the Atlantic Alliance's defensive planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within this scheme certain warheads would be under a commander for use by nuclear-capable NATO forces; part of broader U.S. proposal to supply weapons and stockpiles as an allied deterrent.

rubrics_metrics.name: NATO: make intermediate-range ballistic missiles available to allies
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. will make intermediate range ballistic missiles available to other NATO countries to be used in agreement with alliance planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery of IRBMs 'as soon as the NATO nations in which they would be deployed are ready to receive them.' Meant to integrate missile capabilities into alliance defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: NATO board of top scientists, engineers and production experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a NATO board of top scientists, engineers and production experts, subordinate to the NATO Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board would recommend suitable weapons systems for production, decide what countries should produce which weapons, and decide markets for the weapons produced—aimed at streamlined, coordinated armaments production across NATO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing nuclear know-how and modifying the MacMahon Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Call for a 'share-out of nuclear know-how' to permit 'responsible use' of atomic weapons and for working toward a modification of the MacMahon Act to permit exchanges of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If working from a common fund of knowledge and assumptions about available military force, NATO can better develop plans for effective and discriminating use of nuclear weapons; policy change requires U.S. legislative (Congressional) authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close liaison among NATO and other defense alliances (without merger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Call for close liaison among NATO and such other defense alliances as the Baghdad Pact, SEATO and the Organization of American States, while explicitly not proposing any merger or extension of NATO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask NATO Secretary General to explore means of close cooperation and liaison to coordinate global defense efforts and planning among non-merged alliances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of a NATO science advisor and science scholarships
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint a science advisor to NATO's Secretary General to pool scientific know-how and pledge U.S. contribution of 500 annual science scholarships for students in all alliance members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to overcome and surpass the Soviet Union in scientific and technical capability and to build long-term scientific cooperation within the alliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. seek Congressional authority for joint nuclear propulsion/power programs
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. would seek congressional authority to allow government cooperation with interested NATO members in the development/production and fueling of nuclear propulsion and power plants for submarines and other military purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This would facilitate cooperation in nuclear propulsion and also aid peaceful uses such as nuclear merchant ship propulsion; requires legislative action in the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical advisory group in NATO to study disarmament
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up a technical advisory group in NATO to keep up a continuous study of disarmament and closely study means to end the armaments race while assuring security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The group should 'leave no stone unturned' in the search for an agreement that would end the armaments race while assuring the security of the free world; will report and advise Alliance leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. pledge to immediate assistance to any NATO nation subjected to armed attack
rubrics_metrics.description: Presidential assurance that the United States would come 'at once and with all appropriate force' to the assistance of any NATO nation subjected to armed attack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public, solemn guarantee intended to reassure allies and strengthen deterrence; part of U.S. opening policy statement to the summit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Von Braun/Medaris: urgent technical milestones for space control
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical/strategic requirement that the U.S. achieve major rocket/space milestones (e.g., develop a million-pound thrust engine by 1961; have a manned flight within 5 years and a manned space station within 10 years) to avoid losing control of outer space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues for a 10-year program aimed at control of space; stresses current U.S. shortfalls (largest planned engines ~300,000 pounds thrust) vs. reported Soviet designs (e.g., 820,000 pounds); frames space control as vital to national survival and requires accelerated technical effort and funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance/leadership criterion for missile program ('sundowners')
rubrics_metrics.description: Call for replacement of missile program civilian leadership with men who run a taut organization—'sundowners'—who make hard, firm decisions and bring urgency to missile programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism that decisions 'got lost somewhere in the Defense Department' and that the program needs leaders who will make firm decisions at high levels to speed development; a management/organizational criterion for program success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: transfer missile development to civilian control / Manhattan-like project
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to take missile development from the military services and put it under civilian control, possibly via a Manhattan-like project for rocketry development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim is to improve coordination, speed, and centralized decision-making similar to the atomic bomb project; accompanied by calls for more cooperation and coordination and skepticism that mere creation of advisory posts is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution on arming allies with U.S. nuclear weapons
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy caution that transferring U.S. nuclear weapons to allied countries could increase the risk of local use and escalation into global war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senators expressed that it would 'take a great deal of convincing' to support legislation removing the ban on transfer of U.S. nuclear weapons; risk assessment criterion weighing deterrence benefits vs. proliferation/use risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for missile test site selection (Cape Canaveral vs Pacific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors considered in evaluating whether to move missile testing from Cape Canaveral to the mid-Pacific: secrecy benefits vs. logistical obstacles and lack of closely linked range of islands and facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obstacles include the chain of needed tracking/logistics bases, long distances (e.g., to Ascension, Gilbert islands), supply/shuttle problems for technicians and equipment, and overall impracticality despite secrecy advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful study and postponement before basing nuclear rockets in Europe
rubrics_metrics.description: Several NATO leaders urged 'very thorough study' and recommended postponing final decisions on basing nuclear rockets in Europe, deferring decisions possibly until next spring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates caution and further consultation among alliance members before taking irreversible basing steps; balance urgency against political and strategic ramifications in Europe.
